MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  AUGUST l4, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 5:45 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:46 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated litigation

  1.  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section
  54956.9
  Number of cases: (1)

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 14, 2023
  Page 2 of 14

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy,
  Environmental Sustainability Director; Richard Mollica, Flaming Director; Rob DuBoux,
  Public Works Director; and Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  John Mazza led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:45 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(4), with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council discussed the items
  on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  August 3, 2023, with the amended agenda posted on August 11, 2023.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring moved to approve the agenda.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Grisanti seconded the motion and moved to adjourn the meeting
  in memory of long-time Malibu resident Almette O’Malley.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Riggins moved to also adjourn the meeting in support of the
  residents of Maui and the islands of Hawaii.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Silverstein moved to remove Item No. 4.A. and to reorder the agenda to hear
  Item Nos. 7.A. and 7.B. after Item No. 6.C.

  The amendments were accepted by the maker and the seconder of the motion.

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation of 2023 Jake Kurediian Citizenship Award

  Parks and Recreation Commission Chair Dane Skophammer presented the 2023
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes ofAugust 14, 2023
  ‘  Page 3 of 14

  Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award to Larry Wan on behalf of Sara Wan.

  Mr. Wan thanked the Council for recognizing Ms. Wan for her contributions.

  Presentation on Covote Response Plans

  Rebecca Dmytryk, Humane Wildlife Control, provided a presentation on Coyote
  Response Plans.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Ted Nordblum introduced himself and discussed his campaign for State Assembly
  in District 42 and requested the community’s support.

  Mario Sandoval, Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA),
  presented Malibu Barbie camping playsets to the Councilmembers on behalf of Joe
  Edminston. He discussed the lack of public campgrounds in Malibu.

  Hans Laetz discussed the Wildfires on Maui and emergency alerts that were not
  heard due to power outages. He stated KBUU was looking into the software system
  Alert FM that would transmit emergency alerts originating from the City using
  KBUU’s FM radio frequency to emergency radio devices during an emergency
  which also worked with California’s earthquake alert system. He stated that the
  system was dependent on KBUU having a strong radio signal and discussed the
  need for a radio booster in eastern Malibu for emergency communications.

  Norm Haynie discussed the special event permit for a wedding at 31100 Broad
  Beach Road. He stated that'the set up and teardown for the event was now expected
  to be completed during the eight-hour event timeframe, whereas previously, it was
  planned to be completed in the days before and after the event. He stated that event
  arrangements were made with the previous policy in mind which conflicted with
  the new interpretation and would be highly impactful to the event hosts and guests.

  Dane Skophammer thanked staff and the Council for their work on the temporary
  snack shack at Bluffs Park and requested continued support for the permanent
  snack shack proj ect.

  Kraig Hill discussed emergency preparedness and awareness in advance of fire
  season. He stated that firefighting helicopters were available in southern California
  year-round, with pilots standing by around the clock. He discussed the fire on Maui
  and the importance of backup generators for water pumps located where they were'
  effective and not shifted around. He requested an update on underground placement
  of power lines, covered conductors, and insulated power lines.

  Terry Davis discussed correspondence related to fire preparedness. She stated that
  radio reception was not available in Big Rock even with additional enhanced
  antennas, and additional measures were needed including an evacuation plan. She
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 14, 2023
  Page 4 of 14

  discussed improved flre prevention regulations and better enforcement of codes.
  She stated that she observed an unpermitted party on July 4, 2023 in Big Rock while
  on arson watch and another party was held on the property the past weekend.

  Tim Pera, MRCA, presented the ranger report for the past two months and stated
  that ten citations were issued at La Chuza Beach for dogs on the beach and
  possession of alcohol, and 12 citations at Escondido Canyon for illegal off-trail use.
  He stated they patrolled for illegal parking and cited as needed, and that no
  homeless encampments were observed. He stated that one service call was
  generated which involved signage concerns.

  Stuart Halperin discussed overgrown brush between Bluffs Park and Malibu Road
  which blocked a hiking path. He stated that he contacted the City, who referred him
  to the MRCA, who indicated they would try to help, but after many months, it was
  not addressed.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary stated staff that was working with the grant writing firm
  Townsend Public Affairs. He provided an update on underpass access to Zuma
  Beach and stated that it was still closed due to flooding and signage was placed that
  alerted visitors to use the left turn lane. He provided an update on the Malibu High
  School proj ect and stated that the City was working with the Santa Monica-Malibu
  Unified School District and the California Coastal Commission (CCC). He reported
  that Bluffs Park playground was closed that week for maintenance. He announced
  the summer movie series would conclude on August 19, 2023 at Bluffs Park with
  a screening of The Karate Kid. He announced the Shifting Tides art exhibit would
  conclude on August 25, 2023. He announced that the Baker Tilly development
  services review would be presented at the August 28, 2023 City Council meeting.
  He stated that the School Safety Report was complete and being reviewed by school
  district officials and a summary would be presented at the September 11, 2023
  Council meeting. He thanked the public speakers for their comments on the f1res
  on Maui and stated that thoughts and prayers were with those impacted. He
  commented on emergency preparedness in advance of the National Preparedness
  Month of September. He encouraged community preparation for wildfire season
  and stated that information was available on the City’s website. He announced a
  free structure availability assessment training Would be held on August 30 and 3 1,
  2023. He stated that home wildfire hardening assessments were available through
  the City’s Public Safety Department. He announced a Firewise workshop would be
  held on August l7, 2023 in Camarillo. He stated that there were new evacuation
  zone maps for Malibu, and that informational cards would be mailed to all
  households. He encouraged residents to take the disaster preparedness survey
  available on the City’s website through August 31, 2023. He announced weekly
  tests of the Everbridge disaster notification system during the month of September.
  He welcomed Deputy City Manager Alexis Brown to the City.

  Deputy City Manager Brown stated that she was excited to work for the City and
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 14, 2023
  Page 5 of 14

  looked forward to working with the Council and staff to move initiatives forward.

  City Manager McClary discussed the incident that occurred outside of Nobu
  restaurant on July 4, 2023. He reported that Code Enforcement staff met with the
  owners and managers, it was determined that a Violation occurred, a citation was
  issued, and staff made it clear to them that further incidents would not be tolerated
  and apprised them of event permitting requirements.

  Captain Jennifer Seetoo, Los Angeles County Sheriff s Department, discussed the
  unpermitted event at Nobu on July 4, 2023 and follow-up actions taken by the
  SheriffDepartment, which included Nobu entering into a contract with the Sheriff s
  Department for traffic and parking enforcement. She discussed the screening of a
  documentary on the 201 8 fire that destroyed the town of Paradise, California. She
  discussed the importance of evacuation and communication, and the need for
  utilizing everything they c0u1d for preparation. She discussed new fire
  preparedness supplies for Sheriff’s Deputies. She discussed preparations for red
  flag days which might include closures of parks and trails and local resident only
  access to certain areas. She discussed the Malibu substation Which was awaiting a
  use permit and stated that she was working with the City Manager on innovative
  solutions to staffing issues.
Jtmn  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Uhring, Captain Seetoo stated that once the contract
  was signed, patrols at Nobu would begin with eight—hour shifts on Fridays and
  Saturdays for two weeks and then be reassessed. She stated that Nobu would
  contact her when they planned events to help determine if a permit was required.
  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Stewart, she stated that she would research if the
  City’s handheld units or Sheriff‘s Department tablets would be used for citations.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated that using the City’s handheld units would allow for
  performance review and providing a record of multiple offenders.
  In response to Mayor Silverstein, Captain Seetoo stated that the Sheriff’s
  Department was not involved in the conversation about the communications tower
  and that the City Manager’s office was scheduled to meet on Thursday with the Los
  Angeles County Board of Supervisors and did not know ifthe station was precluded
  from opening until the matter was resolved. She stated that she did not have
  additional information on the body that was found in the lagoon.

  Councilmember Riggins thanked her and expressed her appreciation for her
  professionalism and leadership.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, provided the
  July 2023 part one crime statistics, which were 266 year-to-date, as compared to
  292 at the same time the year prior. He related notable incidents with the common
  theme that suspects were not Malibu residents. He reported an arrest for robbery,
  aggravated assault, and theft of a catalytic converter on PCH, with one suspect still
  at large. He reported an arrest of a suspect for assault of a juvenile relative. He
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 14, 2023
  Page 6 of 14

  reported an arrest for theft, trespassing, and possession of drug paraphernalia on
  Broad Beach Road. He reported that there were flve incidents of petty theft at a
  Malibu Road business, which included shoplifting of beauty products, a hat, and
  food items, and no arrests were made. He reported an incident that occurred on
  Fernhill Drive on July 24, 2023,‘where a suspect broke into a rental home was taken
  into custody after multiple deputies, a K-9 unit, and a SheriffDepartment helicopter
  were deployed. He reported that the beach team would work seven days a week
  through the Labor Day weekend and would work the Chili Cookoff event along
  with their special enforcement deputies. In response to Mayor Pro Tem Uhring, he
  stated that there was an active investigation into the burglary on Portshead Road.
  In response to Mayor Silverstein, he stated that there were two incidents that
  involved helicopters. He stated that an incapacitated person was rescued from the
  ocean off Point Dume with the assistance of a Fire Department helicopter, and the
  Fernhill Drive incident that occurred on July 24, 2023 involved a Sheriff
  Department helicopter.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Riggins stated that she attended an installation dinner for the Los
  Angeles County representative for the League of California Cities. She reported
  that she attended a school district separation mediation. She inquired if the City
  should look into providing flre preparedness supplies to Volunteers on Patrol
  (VOP) and Sheriff Department deputies who patrolled Malibu, similar to what the
  City of Calabasas did as reported by Captain Seetoo. She inquired if the City had
  the ability to push text and email alerts to residents and visitors with evacuation
  information. She stated that she supported camping and discussed campgrounds
  that surrounded the City.

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he attended the League of California Cities with
  Councilmember Riggins, and more information would be included in the upcoming
  ad hoc committee report. He stated that he attended a school separation mediation.
  He stated he spoke to residents concerned about summer traffic. He stated that he
  attended meetings featuring David Revell on lagoon remediation and the Topanga
  Ranch proj ect.

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin confirmed that a
  brief update that an ad hoc meeting was held could be provided during Council
  Comments.

  Councilmember Stewart discussed the City’ s valet ordinance, which required safety
  vests and requested additional enforcement. He discussed incidents at Nobu and
  Big Rock and requested capacity limits be enforced. He stated Malibu was open to
  visitors and had 1.7 million visitors to the beaches in July. He commended the City
  on the temporary snack shack project. He discussed the importance of reflective
  blue fire hydrant markers and acknowledged the City for installation and
  encouraged residents of private streets to have them installed. He discussed the
  importance of backup generators for water pumps and traffic signals. He
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 14, 2023
  Page 7 of 14

  commented on Alert FM and stated that emergency alerts needed to be followed up
  with information on what action the public should take during the emergency, and
  suggested the City apply for a grant. He commented on the tragedy of the fires on
  Maui and stated that the City should do what it could to help.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring discussed the fires on Maui and how easy it was to be
  unprepared for emergencies. He stated that the City had a full schedule of
  community preparedness events during September for National Preparedness
  Month and information was available on the website. He commented on the
  importance of emergency notifications. He commented on unpermitted events at
  Nobu and Big Rock and stated that violation fines were too low and were not an
  effective deterrent. He discussed the farmers’ market which currently operated at
  Legacy Park and stated residents wanted it continued there. He stated useful
  information on development services would be provided by the Baker Tilly report.
  He congratulated Poison Free Malibu on their non-native plant removal event at the
  headlands and commented on restrictions placed upon the volunteers by State Parks
  and requested with them for a discussion on options.

  Mayor Silverstein discussed the unpermitted event held at Nobu. He read an email
  about code violation penalties that he sent to the City Manager shortly after the
  Nobu event and the party at Big Rock occurred. He proposed the formation of an
  ad hoc committee for fine and violation penalty review.‘

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to consider forming
  an Ad Hoc Committee to review Code Enforcement fines and penalties.

  Mayor Silverstein discussed the Item No. 4.A. appeal item that was withdrawn and
  how it was the second time an appeal of the project was withdrawn after
  considerable preparations were made by the Council to hear the item. He stated that
  he participated in meetings with California Strategies. He stated that he met with
  residents who believed their constructiOn issues with neighbors were not adequately
  addressed by the City, but after speaking with staff he learned the issues were being
  addressed, but information was not conveyed to the parties involved and
  encouraged better communication. He stated that he received a call from Supervisor
  Lindsey Horvath’s offlce about a grant opportunity which resulted in Item No. 7.B.
  being on the evening’s meeting agenda.

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated that people
  were not prevented from making a pitch for public office during public comment if
  they were within the City’s jurisdiction.

  Mayor Silverstein thanked Mr. Sandoval for the offer of the Malibu Barbie playset,
  but requested that it be donated to charity, as he did not accept gins. He stated that
  there was abundant camping in the Malibu area. He stated that the Alert FM system
  sounded like it would be valuable in an emergency and he hoped the City would
  get moving on it.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 14, 2023
  Page 8 of 14

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, City Manager McClary stated that would research
  the wedding permitting matter and follow up with public speaker Mr. Haynie.

  Mayor Silverstein stated he was interested if there was a recent policy change in
  permitting events.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring stated that individuals who had not completed their brush
  clearance could be anonymously reported to the Fire Safety Liaisons.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item No. 3.B.5. was pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Uhring seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item No. 3.B.5. The question was called,
  and the motion carried unanimously, Councilmembers Riggins and Stewart
  abstaining from Item No. 3.B.3.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full
  ‘ reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  2.  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  69692-69934 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 729 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $ 2,544,705.63. City of Malibu payroll check number 5356-5365and
  ACH deposits were issued in the amount of $ 1,71 1,453.47.
  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the June 13, 2022 Malibu
  City Council Regular meeting, June 27, 2022 Malibu City Council Regular
  meeting, July ll, 2022 Malibu City Council Regular meeting, and July 28,
  2022 Malibu City Council Special meeting.
  4.  Findings to Hold Virtual City Council, Commission, Committee, Board and
  Other City Bodies, Meetings Under AB 361
  Recommended Action: Consider a motion to reaffirm Resolution No. 23-
  14, re-authorizing remote teleconferencing/virtual meetings pursuant to AB
  361.
  6.  Amendment to Art Loan Agreement with Artist Anna Kelly
  Recommended Action: Approve the recommendation from the Malibu Arts
  Commission to accept Amendment No. 1 to the Art Loan Agreement with
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes ofAugust 14, 2023
  Page 9 of 14

  Artist Anna Kelly to display her artwork Saving Malibu through August 25,
  2023.
  7.  Amendment to Professional Services Agreement with Civic Solutions
  Recommended Action: Authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment
  No. 1 to the Professional Services Agreement with Civic Solutions, Inc. for
  contract planning services.

  The following item was pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  5.  Investment Report for the Month Ending June 30, 2023
  Recommended Action: Receive the Investment Report for the month
  ending June 30, 2023.

  Assistant City Manager Toney presented the staff report.

  The Council discussed the item.

  The Council received the Investment Report for the month ending June 30,
  2023.

ITEM 4  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  Appeal No. 23-001 — Appeal of Flaming Commission Resolution No. 23-02 (3620
  Noranda Lane; Owner: 3620 Noranda Lane, LLC)
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 23-37, determining the proj ect is
  categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),
  denying Appeal No. 23 -001 and approving Coastal Development Permit (CDP) No.
  17-104 for the construction of a new single-family residence, a basement including
  a subterranean garage, a new onsite wastewater treatment system (OWTS), exterior
  site improvements including a new swimming pool, spa, deck, landscape,
  hardscape, and grading; including Variance (VAR) No. 19-035 to allow for
  development within the required Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Area (ESHA)
  buffer, Site Plan Review (SPR) No. 23-003 for development on slopes steeper than
  3 to 1, but flatter than 2.5 to l, Minor Modification (MM) No. 20-012 for the
  reduction of the required front yard setback by up to 50 percent, and Offer-to-
  Dedicate (OTD) No. 23-001 for a trail easement, for the property located in the
  Rural Residential-Five Acre (RR-5) zoning district at 3620 Noranda Lane (3620
  Noranda Lane, LLC).

  This item was removed from the agenda upon approval of the agenda.

ITEM 5  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS

  Woolsev Fire Fee Waiver Program Update
  Recommended Action: Receive and flle an update on the Woolsey Fire Fee Waiver
  Program.

  Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Ryan Embree

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions t0 staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion
  to bring back an item to consider extending the Woolsey Fire Fee Waiver Program.

  The motion was withdrawn.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council: 1) received and filed an update on the Woolsey Fire Fee
  Waiver Program, and 2) directed staff to bring back an item to consider extending
  the Woolsey Fire Fee Waiver Program.

  Bovs & Girls Club of Malibu Event Fee Waiver
  Recommended Action: Consider Whether to approve the request from the Malibu
  Foundation for Youth and Families, DBA-Boys & Girls Club of Malibu to waive
  facility use fees and staffing costs for the Chili Cook-Off event at the Ioki Property.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Kasey Earnest and Ryan Embree

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion to
  approve the request from the Malibu Foundation for Youth and Families, DBA
  Boys & Girls Club of Malibu to waive facility use fees and staffing costs for the
  Chili Cook-Off event at the Ioki Property.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 14, 2023
  Page 11 of 14

  The Council discussed the motion and directed questiOns to staff.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  At 8:45 p.m., Mayor Silverstein recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:57
  pm. with all Councilmembers present.

  Malibu Farmers Market Fee Waiver
  Recommended Action: Consider whether to approve the request from the
  Comucopia Foundation to waive the facility use and permit fees for the Malibu
  Farmers Market at Legacy Park.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to the table for discussion.
  The Council discussed the item and. directed questions to staff.

  MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Uhring seconded a motion to
  approve the request from the Cornucopia Foundation to waive the facility use and
4L  permit fees for the Malibu Farmers Market at Legacy Park.
  The Council discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

  The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Councilmember Grisanti
  abstaining.

  ITEM 7  COUNCIL ITEMS

  Designation of Voting Delegate and Alternate Voting Delegate(s) for the 2023
  League of Califomia Cities Annual Conference
  Recommended Action: Designate the City’s voting delegate and altemate voting
  delegate(s) for the League of Califomia Cities 2023 Annual Conference scheduled
  for September 20-22, 2023 in Sacramento.

  City Manager McClary presented the staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Silverstein retumed the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item.

  MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion
  to designate Councilmember Riggins as the voting delegate, and Councilmember
  Grisanti as the altemate voting delegate for the League of Califomia Cities 2023
  Annual Conference. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  Los An eles Coun National Oceanic and Atmos heric Administration OAA
  Climate Resilience Regional Challenge — SUPPORT (Mavor Silverstein)
  Recommended Action: At the request of Mayor Silverstein, authorize the City to
  partner with Los Angeles County in pursuing the NOAA Climate Resilience
  Regional Challenge competitive funding opportunity as a co-applicant.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Zachary Gaidzik

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item.

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion
  to authorize the City to partner with Los Angeles County in pursuing the NOAA
  Climate Resilience Regional Challenge competitive funding opportunity as a co-
  applicant.

  The Council discussed the motion and directed questions to Mr. Gaidzik.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS (CONTINUED)

  Proposed Settlement Agreement with Cross Creek Ranch Malibu, LLC gCCRM)
